relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a Chinese girl with Blau syndrome carrying a NOD2 variant: "a heterozygous T605P variant (c.1813 A > C, De novo) in the NOD2 gene".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script only assembled the JSON from hand-chosen values and spans. One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5; Table 1's 'Case' in the Patient column is a role word, not a label). The Case report paragraphs from 'This patient visited our hospital again in August 2022' to 'is doing well on follow up' are printed twice in the Markdown, with small differences. Contradiction: IVIG dose is '1g/kg each time*twice' in the first copy and '2 g/kg each time*twice' in the second; treatment_summary quotes the second copy. The paper prints 'De novo' beside the variant but describes no parental testing, so inheritance is left 'not reported' under rule 8/D-24 and parental_testing_statement is 'not reported'. Variant type not stated (only 'variant'/'mutation'), so not reported. Age at diagnosis taken as the age at first presentation (4 years), when the diagnosis was confirmed per the same paragraph; the Abstract says diagnosis was '6 years ago' at age 10. 'Ocular symptoms were not found' recorded as an excluded feature; uveitis left 'not reported' on the checklist (symptoms vs examination), and visual impairment also left 'not reported'. 'negative vascular ultrasonography' is a normal investigation as a whole; recorded as 'abnormal vascular ultrasonography' excluded, and the vasculitis checklist item left 'not reported'. Normal brain CT/MRI and negative serum pathogen tests recorded as excluded at the level the paper names. 'joint movement disorder' was absent at first presentation (2017) while 'multiple joint activity limits' were observed from June 2022; these are different time points, not a contradiction. Neurological features (GBS, 2023) are attributed by the authors to TNF inhibitor (Yisaipu) treatment; the facial findings and peripheral nerve damage are recorded under the checklist item 'cranial or other neuropathy (facial palsy)' as observed although they are part of GBS, not attributed to Blau syndrome itself. Table 2 is a group-level literature summary (counts only; includes 'our case') and gives no individual rows. Supplementary material is only the CARE checklist.
